_meta.indication: In combination with dexamethasone for the treatment of adult patients with relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma (RRMM) who have received at least four prior therapies and whose disease is refractory to at least two proteasome inhibitors, at least two immunomodulatory agents, and an anti-CD38 monoclonal antibody

pivotal_trials.nct: Not stated in the reviewed documents
pivotal_trials.design: Multicenter, open-label, single-arm trial of selinexor 80 mg twice weekly in combination with dexamethasone 20 mg twice weekly; treatment continued until disease progression, unacceptable toxicity, or death
pivotal_trials.population: Part 2 enrolled 123 patients with RRMM who had received at least three prior lines of therapy and whose disease was refractory to at least one proteasome inhibitor, at least one immunomodulatory agent, and an anti-CD38 monoclonal antibody; accelerated approval was based on the BCLPD-refractory subgroup of 83 patients who had received at least four prior therapies and whose disease was refractory to at least two PIs, at least two IMiDs, and an anti-CD38 mAb
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Overall response rate (ORR), the proportion of patients with a PR or better, assessed by an Independent Review Committee per IMWG criteria
pivotal_trials.n: Part 2 enrolled 123 patients; the modified-intent-to-treat (mITT) population comprised 122 patients, and accelerated approval was based on the BCLPD-refractory subgroup of 83 patients
pivotal_trials.result: In the BCLPD-refractory subgroup (N=83), ORR was 25.3% (95% CI: 16.4%, 36%) with median DOR of 3.8 months (range 0.7, 8.1). In the overall mITT Part 2 population (122 patients), ORR was 25.4% (95% CI: 18%, 34.1%) with median DOR of 4.4 months.

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (incidence >=20%): thrombocytopenia, fatigue, nausea, anemia, decreased appetite, decreased weight, diarrhea, vomiting, hyponatremia, neutropenia, leukopenia, constipation, dyspnea, and upper respiratory tract infection. In STORM Part 2, all patients (100%) had a TEAE, 60.2% had a serious TEAE, and 8.1% had a fatal TEAE.
target_moa: Selinexor is a first-in-class, oral, small molecule inhibitor of the nuclear export protein exportin 1 (XPO1); XPO1 inhibition is hypothesized to restore normal tumor suppressor pathways and lead to selective apoptosis of neoplastic cells

advisory_committee.vote: The application was presented at an Oncologic Drugs Advisory Committee (ODAC) meeting on February 26, 2019; the committee voted in favor of delaying consideration of approval until results of the randomized phase 3 BOSTON trial are available

summary.text: XPOVIO (selinexor), a first-in-class oral XPO1 inhibitor with orphan designation for multiple myeloma, was reviewed under Priority review and granted accelerated approval based on the ORR observed in the single-arm STORM trial. Because ORR reflects only a short-term benefit, the ongoing phase 3 BOSTON trial (KCP-330-023) was required as the confirmatory trial to verify clinical benefit. An ODAC meeting was convened and voted to delay approval pending BOSTON results.
